answer: An applicant posts a 25-unit refundable deposit and reserves one meadow plot for 48 hours. Every twenty minutes it publishes a nectar receipt H(job-salt || plot-key || minute-bucket) and grinds a 30-minute VDF, blocking burst precomputation. A canyon gate allows one crossing per plot-key each week, countersigned by two raters from different drainage basins. Shared plot-keys, or an 8-bit prefix collision in over a third of receipts, burn the deposit and blacklist the plot for fourteen days. Cloned keys inherit the drip pattern, so aliases raise VDF cost and forfeited stake, not cheap logins.
